title: sync: opportunistic responses not consumed on postEventually/RequestVault path
description: Sync.consumeIncomingResponse only runs via wrapHandlersForSync, which is applied in Rest.post/get/put/patch/delete (rest.js). But trackEvent -> Events.sendEvent defaults to Rest.postEventually (events.js:252) -> Request.requestEventually -> RequestVault (rest.js:443, embassy request.js:257), sent with NO handlers. So the _contactSync block on POST /v1/events responses is never consumed on the default event path; opportunistic sync only works for callers that postImmediately. Confirmed in-browser 2026-06-15: WonderPush.trackEvent('foo') did not trigger the explicit contact fetch until events.js was locally hacked to use Rest.post. FIX: run consumeIncomingResponse on the RequestVault flush response too (trace how RequestVaultJob surfaces its response in embassy). ACCEPTANCE: trackEvent('foo') with default (postEventually) path consumes _contactSync from the /events response and triggers the explicit fetch.
close_reason: Fixed in commit (rest.js): RequestVaultJob.prototype.run wrapped with wrapHandlersForSync so postEventually/vault responses run through Sync.consumeIncomingResponse. Verify in-browser with default trackEvent (no events.js hack).

title: inapp: merge synced popups (sdk-sync popups source) into in-app campaign evaluation
description:
Consume the synced popups list (sdk-sync 'popups' source, stored by fpk) in the in-app engine ALONGSIDE the remote-config campaigns. This is the engine-consumption step fpk/ki1 deferred ('transport only').

Each stored PopupItem carries data: Campaign (the popup rule). In main.ts triggerEvent, after fetching inAppConfig.campaigns, also fetch Sync.getSourceData('popups'), extract the Campaign from each NON-tombstone, non-expired item (status !== 'deleted' && expirationDate >= now), and concat those onto inAppConfig.campaigns before building CampaignWrappers. Synced popups are individualized rules expected to be DISJOINT from the global config (sources.md:149), so plain concatenation (no dedupe) — remote-config first, then synced. Best-effort + null-safe (Sync may be absent; getSourceData never rejects). Gated naturally by the @APP_OPEN sync-settle wait (bd 86i) so the freshly-synced list is used.

Out of scope: per-campaign precedence/sorting between the two sources, dedupe-by-campaignId.
acceptance_criteria: 1. On a trigger, synced non-deleted/non-expired popups' Campaigns are evaluated by the same segment/capping/trigger pipeline as remote-config campaigns. 2. Tombstones (status=='deleted') and expired items are excluded. 3. When no popups are synced / Sync absent, behavior is exactly as today. 4. Touched code typechecks; existing inapp tests pass.
notes: Touch point: src/inappmessaging/main.ts triggerEvent Promise.all + campaignWrappers build. Depends on fpk (storage) + uses Sync.getSourceData('popups'). PopupItem.data: Campaign (sync-popups-store.ts). Origin: user request 2026-06-24.
close_reason: Implemented in this commit. PopupItem.data typed as Campaign; main.ts triggerEvent fetches Sync.getSourceData('popups') and concatenates each non-deleted/non-expired item's data Campaign onto inAppConfig.campaigns before CampaignWrapper build. Tombstones+expired excluded; null-safe; disjoint plain-concat (no dedupe). Typecheck clean, 39 inapp tests pass. Test gap: behavioral test needs a triggerEvent/InAppMessaging harness (none exists) — deferred, same as 86i.

title: merge notiflex-segmentation-dsl-parser ContactSource branch into master + re-pin SDK
description:

It was kept on a branch partly to coordinate with notiflex-segmentation-dsl-esquery (the other parser consumer) — but esquery serves no purpose, so there is no consumer left to coordinate with and no reason to keep ContactSource off master.

Also note: the SDK pins f0e716 ('suffix and contains'), which is ONE commit AHEAD of the parser's master. So master is itself behind the SDK's pinned base. Merging should also bring suffix/contains onto master (or confirm it lands) so master stops lagging what the SDK actually uses.

Steps:

2. Open an MR for 2way-sync-contact-source -> master (this carries f0e716 'suffix and contains' + a7844de ContactSource). Get it reviewed/merged.
3. Re-pin wonderpush-javascript-sdk package.json + yarn.lock from the branch hash (a7844de) to the merged master commit.
4. Delete the 2way-sync-contact-source branch after merge.
5. (Optional) since esquery is purposeless, consider archiving/decommissioning it so future parser changes don't carry phantom-consumer caveats.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ContactSource (and suffix/contains) is on parser master.
2. SDK pins a master commit, not the feature-branch hash; yarn.lock matches; tests still green.
3. The 2way-sync-contact-source branch is deleted.
4. esquery's status (dead/archived) is recorded so the cross-consumer caveat is formally retired.
notes: Parser branch: 2way-sync-contact-source @ a7844deb25e4afbf8466c9d53ecca62fb8b24627 (gitlab.com/wonderpush/notiflex-segmentation-dsl-parser). SDK consumer: wonderpush-javascript-sdk (5ar). The optional visitContactSource was chosen specifically to avoid breaking esquery's build; if esquery is gone, a required method would also have been fine, but optional is harmless to keep. Origin: user note 2026-06-23 that esquery serves no purpose.
close_reason: ContactSource merged to parser master via fast-forward (f0e7163..a7844de, user-authorized direct FF push since esquery is confirmed purposeless and no MR review was needed). origin/master now carries suffix/contains + ContactSource. Branch 2way-sync-contact-source deleted (remote + local); local master synced. SDK already pins a7844de, which is now a master commit, so no re-pin needed; yarn.lock matches; 206 SDK tests green. title: sync: verify + lock opportunistic injection coverage on the Measurements API /events
description:
The sdk-sync spec includes the Measurements API in scope (the unauthenticated branch of identifier loading in algorithm.md). We must piggyback sync params on Measurements API calls too.

Current state (verified by code reading 2026-06-22):
- OUTGOING injection ALREADY happens on Measurements /events: events.js:236-253 sends via the same Rest.post/postEventually/postBeacon with the full measurements URL (rest.js getUrl passthrough, rest.js:22). addCommonParams (rest.js:269) calls Sync.prepareOutgoingParams (rest.js:295), gated by shouldInjectForPath (sync-outgoing.ts:19) which matches ANY path ending in '/events' — so the measurements host URL passes.
- INCOMING processing covered for post (wrapHandlersForSync) and postEventually (el1 RequestVault wrap); NOT postBeacon (response-less — universal, not measurements-specific).

BUT this coverage is incidental (suffix match), untested, and not end-to-end verified for the measurements-specific send path / backend handling.

This task: turn 'incidental + probably works' into 'verified + locked'.

Steps:
1. Confirm end-to-end that a Measurements API /events POST carries the _<source>Sync.* params and that the measurements backend returns/echoes _<source>Sync blocks that the SDK consumes (coordinate w/ measurements-api if needed).
2. Verify the incoming response from the measurements send variant actually reaches Sync.consumeIncomingResponse (which variant does trackInternalEventWithMeasurementsApi use — postImmediately => Rest.post => wrapHandlersForSync?).
3. Add regression tests: shouldInjectForPath matches a full measurements /events URL; a measurements post injects the sync block; (if feasible) the response is consumed.
4. Document the postBeacon limitation (no response => no incoming sync) explicitly.
5. Decide whether the suffix-match gate should EXPLICITLY allow measurements (intentional) vs tightening it — make the intent unambiguous in code + comment.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A test asserts shouldInjectForPath returns true for the canonical measurements /events URL.
2. A test (or documented manual verification) shows a measurements /events request carries _<source>Sync.* params.
3. Incoming consumption from the measurements path is confirmed (or the gap documented if a variant like beacon can't).
4. Code/comment makes the measurements coverage intentional, not accidental.
5. postBeacon response-less limitation documented.
notes: Origin: user requirement 2026-06-22 (piggyback measurements). Spec: algorithm.md unauthenticated/Measurements branch. Touch points: sync-outgoing.ts shouldInjectForPath, rest.js addCommonParams/getUrl/post/postEventually/postBeacon, events.js sendEvent, sdk.js trackInternalEventWithMeasurementsApi.
close_reason: SDK side locked: shouldInjectForPath host-agnostic /events match documented as intentional + regression test for the measurements URL; incoming consumption confirmed by code path (trackInternalEventWithMeasurementsApi posts immediately via Rest.post -> wrapHandlersForSync -> consumeIncomingResponse); beacon response-less limitation documented in rest.js. 168 sync tests pass. Residual (NOT an SDK task): backend confirmation that measurements-api processes _<source>Sync params and echoes _<source>Sync blocks.

title: sync: per-source fetch rate-limit floor (minSourceFetchIntervalMs)
description:
Add a minimum-interval floor between explicit-fetch attempts per source, applied to ALL triggers (firm hint, weak hint, max-age forcing) — not just weak signals. Prevents fetch storms such as the observed max-age-forcing tight loop when a server returns a frozen readDate (lastReadDate never advances => isStateStale always true => checkMaxAgeForcing fires Sync.fetch after every response with no rate limit).

Sync.fetch is the single choke point for all explicit fetches. Today only weak signals are throttled (shouldDebounceWeakSignal) and only failures back off (exponential backoff, reset on success), so a stream of SUCCESSFUL forced fetches is unbounded.

Implementation:
1. sync-knobs.ts: add minSourceFetchIntervalMs to SyncKnobs + DEFAULT_KNOBS (default 2_000; 0 disables). Remote-config overridable like the other knobs.
2. sync-fetch.ts: add pure helper shouldRateLimitSource(now, lastFetchAttemptedDate, minIntervalMs): boolean (true when now - lastFetchAttemptedDate < minIntervalMs and minIntervalMs > 0), mirroring shouldDebounceWeakSignal.
3. sync.js Sync.fetch: after the weak-debounce check and before the mutex tryAcquire, skip silently when shouldRateLimitSource is true. Reuses the already-loaded state.lastFetchAttemptedDate (stamped in runFetchWithMutexHeld step 3, persisted before the GET).

Skip (don't defer): consistent with mutex-busy / weak-debounce. Safe because the chased mark (2rd) only advances on fetch success, so a skipped firm hint re-fires on the next opportunistic response — no data lost, just delayed. This is the per-source half of the rate-limiting proposal (sync-rate-limiting-proposal.md); the global token-bucket limiter and the max-age-forcing cap-cadence gate are deliberately out of scope here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. sync-fetch unit: shouldRateLimitSource true when now-last < interval, false when >=, false when interval<=0, false when lastFetchAttemptedDate==0 (never fetched).
2. A forced (max-age) fetch storm against a frozen-readDate server issues at most one fetch per minSourceFetchIntervalMs per source (covered via sync-pilot or a focused test).
3. Weak debounce and exponential backoff behavior unchanged; firm fetches with genuinely-new hints still occur (just floored).
4. minSourceFetchIntervalMs: 0 fully disables the floor (no behavior change vs today).
notes: Choke point: sync.js Sync.fetch (around the weak-debounce + mutex steps). Pure-helper pattern: sync-fetch.ts shouldDebounceWeakSignal. Companion follow-ups (NOT here): global token-bucket limiter; gate checkMaxAgeForcing on the cap interval so forcing polls at its configured cadence rather than the floor. Origin: the maxLastReadDateAgeMs=5000 storm during pilot testing.
close_reason: Implemented + tested: minSourceFetchIntervalMs knob (default 2000, remote-config key syncMinSourceFetchIntervalMs), shouldRateLimitSource pure helper, wired into Sync.fetch after weak-debounce / before mutex. 173 sync tests pass.

title: sync: implement chased high-water mark to suppress redundant firm fetches
description:
Implement the design recorded on wonderpush-javascript-sdk-ns7 (closed). Stop a firm head hint from re-triggering an explicit fetch once we've already chased that (knownVersion, knownVersionId) to a 'no change confirmed' result.

Steps:
1. sync-state.ts: add lastChasedVersion (number=0) and lastChasedVersionId (number|string|null=null) to SyncSourceState + emptyState(). Local-only; never sent to the server.
2. sync-processor.ts:244-250: gate the firm trigger on the hint being strictly newer than BOTH (lastVersion,lastVersionId) AND (lastChasedVersion,lastChasedVersionId), reusing the existing vCmp/idCmp(compareVersionId) shape.
3. sync.js runFetchWithMutexHeld step 6 (success branch that resets lastFetchUnsuccessfulAttemptCount): if the echoed hint.knownVersion is strictly higher than the current chased mark, adopt (hint.knownVersion, hint.knownVersionId). Hint-less fetches (max-age forcing) must not touch the mark.
4. sync-processor.ts empty-reset branch (version 0 accepted / wipe): reset lastChasedVersion=0, lastChasedVersionId=null.

See ns7 design field for full rationale, candidate comparison, concurrency/persistence notes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. sync-processor unit: with lastChasedVersion=N, a block with knownVersion<=N yields NO triggerFetch; knownVersion=N+1 yields firm.
2. sync-processor unit: empty-reset resets the mark (a subsequent equal hint re-triggers).
3. sync-pilot integration: firm hint -> fetch -> 'no change confirmed' -> a second identical firm hint produces NO second fetch; a strictly-higher hint does.
4. A failed fetch does NOT advance the mark (genuinely-new updates still retried).
5. No new remote-config knob required; existing max-age forcing still re-checks periodically.
notes: Design source: ns7 (closed, see its design field). Pilot: contact (single-object, versionId null). Touch points: sync-state.ts, sync-processor.ts:244-250 + empty-reset branch, sync.js runFetchWithMutexHeld step 6. Inherits the benign fetch-lock vs sync:proc:<source> race (monotonic-max mark).
close_reason: REVERTED — change of heart 2026-06-18. Decision: do NOT suppress firm re-fetches with a chased high-water mark. With the per-source rate limiter (9vn, minSourceFetchIntervalMs) in place, we accept re-fetching on every firm hint and let the limiter bound it nicely (<=1 fetch / interval) rather than carrying the extra per-source state (lastChasedVersion/lastChasedVersionId) + processor/fetch-success/empty-reset complexity. The original ns7 over-query concern is now mitigated by rate-limiting, not by suppression. Implementation 2085654 is being reverted; algorithm.md chased-mark edits reverted too.

title: sync: suppress redundant explicit fetches when a firm hint yields no new data
description:
Design a mechanism to avoid over-querying the server on the explicit-fetch loop.

Concrete repro (contact pilot): a POST /events opportunistic response carries a FIRM head hint — knownVersion > lastVersion (sync-processor.ts:244-249) — so the processor returns triggerFetch:'firm'. Firm signals are deliberately NOT debounced; shouldDebounceWeakSignal (sync-fetch.ts:42-50) only guards weak (knownReadDate-only) signals. The SDK then does GET /contact echoing the hint. But /contact comes back as 'no change confirmed' (version+versionId match): the processor advances lastReadDate and lastSyncDate but NOT lastVersion (sync-processor.ts:206-219).

Result: the very next POST /events that carries the same bumped knownVersion still satisfies knownVersion > lastVersion, so it re-fires a firm fetch. Every subsequent event POST triggers another /contact fetch that returns nothing new — unbounded redundant querying. This happens whenever the channel/profile-level version advances for reasons that don't change a given single-object source (e.g. a different source moved, or events bumped a shared version).

This task is to DEVISE and document the approach (then a follow-up implements it). Candidate directions to evaluate — do not pre-commit:
  1. Track a 'chased' high-water mark in SyncSourceState (e.g. lastChasedVersion/lastChasedVersionId) = the highest head-hint (version, versionId) for which we already issued an explicit fetch. Suppress a firm trigger when (knownVersion, knownVersionId) <= that mark and the fetch already happened. Advance the mark when a fetch is attempted; the existing compareVersionId (sync-versionid.ts) gives the ordering.
  2. Extend the existing debounce to firm signals too (time-window), simpler but coarser — may delay legitimately-new data.
  3. Hybrid: high-water-mark suppression + a max-age force so we still re-check occasionally.
Weigh correctness (must not drop a genuinely-new update), persistence cost (new state field => storage write), and identifier-change interaction (empty-reset must still re-fetch).
design:
MECHANISM: per-source "chased" high-water mark (candidate 1). Candidate 3's periodic re-check comes for free via existing max-age forcing. Candidate 2 rejected (see below).

ROOT CAUSE
The firm-hint gate (sync-processor.ts:244-250) compares head hint knownVersion/knownVersionId against the source's OWN lastVersion/lastVersionId. knownVersion is a coarse "latest version the server has" signal that can climb for reasons unrelated to a single-object source. When an explicit fetch returns "no change confirmed" (sync-processor.ts:208-216), lastVersion is intentionally NOT advanced. So knownVersion > lastVersion stays true and every subsequent POST /events re-fires a firm fetch that returns nothing. Firm signals are not debounced (only weak: sync-fetch.ts:42-50) => unbounded.

NEW STATE FIELDS (sync-state.ts, add to emptyState())
- lastChasedVersion: number = 0
- lastChasedVersionId: number|string|null = null
Local bookkeeping (like lastFetchAttemptedDate); never sent to the server.

TRIGGER GATE (sync-processor.ts:244-250)
Trigger firm iff hint strictly newer than (lastVersion,lastVersionId) AND strictly newer than (lastChasedVersion,lastChasedVersionId). Reuse the file's existing shape: vCmp = known - lastChased; idCmp = compareVersionId(knownVersionId, lastChasedVersionId); newer = vCmp>0 || (vCmp===0 && idCmp>0).

ADVANCE THE MARK ON FETCH SUCCESS, NOT ON TRIGGER (correctness)
Set it only when an explicit fetch completes successfully, in runFetchWithMutexHeld step 6 (sync.js success .then that resets lastFetchUnsuccessfulAttemptCount). The fetch already receives `hint`; if hint.knownVersion present and (hint.knownVersion,hint.knownVersionId) > (lastChasedVersion,lastChasedVersionId), adopt it.
- Failed fetch (network/mutex-busy) => mark NOT advanced => retried (never drops a genuinely-new update).
- Success with new data => lastVersion advances normally; mark advances too (harmless).
- Success "no change confirmed" => lastVersion stays, mark == knownVersion => identical future hints suppressed (the fix).
- Hint-less fetches (max-age forcing: Sync.fetch(source,{})) carry no knownVersion => never touch the mark.

EMPTY-RESET / IDENTIFIER CHANGE (acceptance #4)
In the empty-reset branch (version 0 accepted; existing clearState/wipe path), reset lastChasedVersion=0 / lastChasedVersionId=null. Empty-reset is the SDK's only identity-change signal (it does not inspect meta.identifiers), so resetting keeps re-fetch working across identity switches.

WHY NOT CANDIDATE 2 (debounce firm signals)
Time-window debouncing only reduces frequency; after each window it re-fires and again returns nothing, so it does NOT converge and adds latency to genuinely-new updates. Rejected as primary.

PERIODIC SAFETY NET (candidate 3, free)
checkMaxAgeForcing already issues a firm, hint-LESS Sync.fetch when lastSyncDate/lastReadDate exceed knobs.maxLastSyncDateAgeMs/maxLastReadDateAgeMs (both +Infinity by default). Hint-less fetches bypass the mark, so the "re-check occasionally" property of the hybrid is already provided. No extra code or knob.

CONCURRENCY NOTE (inherited)
Mark is written under the fetch lock (sync:<source>) while normal processing writes state under sync:proc:<source> (commit c9ec1a0). Benign for the mark: it is a monotonic max, so a lost update at worst causes one extra chase, never a dropped update.

PERSISTENCE COST
Two extra fields on an already-persisted struct. The mark write piggybacks on the save step 6 already performs (failure-count reset) — no new round-trip on the hot path. No new knobs.

TEST PLAN (for the implementation follow-up)
- sync-processor unit: with lastChasedVersion=N, a block with knownVersion<=N yields NO triggerFetch; knownVersion=N+1 yields firm.
- sync-processor unit: empty-reset resets the mark (subsequent equal hint re-triggers).
- sync-pilot integration: firm hint -> fetch -> "no change confirmed" -> a second identical firm hint produces no second fetch; a strictly-higher hint does.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A written design (in the issue design field or algorithm.md) specifying the chosen suppression mechanism, the new/changed SyncSourceState fields if any, and where in sync-processor.ts/sync-fetch.ts the decision is made.
2. The design proves the repeated-firm-hint case above issues at most one fetch per distinct (version, versionId) high-water advance, not one per event POST.
3. The design shows a genuinely-newer hint (higher version OR higher versionId) still triggers a fetch.
4. The design shows an empty-reset / identifier change still re-fetches (not suppressed by the high-water mark).
5. Knob-configurable where relevant, consistent with DEFAULT_KNOBS in sync-knobs.ts.
notes: Relevant files: sync-processor.ts (hint -> triggerFetch decision, lines 243-258), sync-fetch.ts (shouldDebounceWeakSignal, buildExplicitFetchParams), sync-versionid.ts (compareVersionId / acceptsResponse ordering), sync-state.ts (SyncSourceState — would host any new high-water field). Part of the sdk-sync epic. Spotted while filing wonderpush-javascript-sdk-bro (clearAllData verification).
close_reason: Design completed and recorded in the design field: per-source 'chased' high-water mark (lastChasedVersion/lastChasedVersionId), gated in sync-processor.ts trigger, advanced on fetch success in sync.js, reset on empty-reset. Implementation tracked as a follow-up.

title: sync: verify clearAllData() clears all sync:* state keys
description:
The 2-way sync (sdk-sync) persists per-source state via SyncState (src/wonderpush/sync-state.ts) under keys shaped 'sync:<source>:<userId>:<deviceId>' (storageKey, sync-state.ts:49-51), backed by WonderPushSDK._protected.Storage (wired in sync.js:70). The public WonderPush#clearAllData() API (sdk.js:939) must wipe all locally-written data, including these sync state keys.

clearAllData -> Data.clearAll() (data.js:230) -> clearAllLocalStorage() (data.js:149), which lists every key-value pair in Storage.getKeyValueStorageStoreName() and bulk-deletes them. In principle this should cover sync:* keys since SyncState uses the same Storage. This task is to PROVE that end-to-end with a regression test, and fix the issues found.

Two latent defects spotted in clearAllLocalStorage (data.js:149-158) that likely break this guarantee:
  1. data.js:156-157: missing '.' before 'then(...)'. ASI parses it as 'return listKeyValuePairs().then(deleteCb);' + a separate dead 'then(...)' statement. The trailing callback never chains.
  2. data.js:153: Storage.bulk(...) result is not returned from the .then(pairs) callback, so clearAll() may resolve BEFORE the deletes complete (if bulk is async).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A regression test registers a sync source, writes state (so a 'sync:<source>:<userId>:<deviceId>' key exists in Storage), calls clearAllData(), and asserts NO 'sync:*' keys remain after the returned promise resolves.
2. The test covers both userId-scoped and anonymous (empty userId) sync keys.
3. clearAllData()'s returned promise does not resolve until all deletes have completed (awaits Storage.bulk).
4. The two clearAllLocalStorage defects (missing-dot chain, unreturned bulk) are fixed or proven harmless.
notes: Pilot context: contact source (single-object). See SyncState/storageKey in sync-state.ts and the in-memory SyncStorage in sync-pilot.test.ts:63-86 for a test harness pattern. Related to the sdk-sync epic (other sync source issues: sfj/g8i/fpk/4ke/8h5).
close_reason: Both clearAllLocalStorage defects fixed in a229aef (unreturned Storage.bulk + missing-dot then chain); clearAllData now awaits its deletes. Regression test (acceptance #1-#3) intentionally skipped per user — no AMD .js test harness exists in this repo.

title: sync: URL/payload size investigation for lastSyncMeta
description: Spike. The algorithm has the SDK echo back the server-issued meta JSON object on every opportunistic call, for each source. 5 sources × ~50-200 bytes = ~1 KB per request just for sync metadata. Some CDNs/proxies start truncating around 8 KB. Options: send via header, send body, or accept. Decide before opportunistic injection ships to production.
design: See plan open-issue #1.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: query-string vs header vs body, with sizing measurement and the chosen path documented for the foundation issue to follow.
close_reason: Decision 2026-06-11 (user call): lastSyncMeta + sync params go in the query string. No measurement done; the user accepted the worst-case math (~1KB/request total for the 5-source case once all sources are wired) as within CDN/proxy URL limits. If we ever exceed limits in practice, revisit by moving lastSyncMeta to a header. Per-source blocks are emitted only for sources the SDK has plug-ins for, so until Session 8 (contact pilot) lands, the per-source addition is zero bytes.

title: sync: contact source plug-in (single-object)

title: sync: explicit fetch loop with mutex + exponential backoff

title: sync: incoming response processor + dispatch from rest.js
description: Read _serverTime and _<source>Sync.* blocks from responses. Dispatch to per-source applyData/applyDelta/clearState callbacks. Implement all 7 response types from algorithm.md: 'no affirmative info' (block missing), 'try asking explicitly' (empty {}), 'weak hint of change' (knownReadDate only), 'firm hint of change' (knownVersion/knownVersionId/knownReadDate), 'no change confirmed', 'no data exists', 'here is the new data'. Apply acceptance check before mutation. On 'here is the new data', apply data first then delta (algorithm.md:190). State-update order: data → delta → version/versionId → readDate → lastSyncDate from _serverTime (algorithm.md:206-210). Multi-object opportunistic responses NEVER carry data/delta — only hints (algorithm.md:120-121). meta is opaque (algorithm.md:316) — store and echo lastSyncMeta without inspection.
design: Hook at the rest.js per-method level — but not at the lines the original plan named. The actual handlers.onload(...) invocations live in embassy/src/embassy/request.js (lines 131, 215-216), which has no path context. So the hook is: in each of this.get / this.post / this.patch / this.delete / this.put / this.postEventually / this.postEventuallyAnonymously / this.postBeacon, BEFORE calling Request.request(..., handlers, ...), wrap handlers.onload with a function that first calls Sync.consumeIncomingResponse(path, method, response) and then forwards to the original handlers.onload (if any). The path is in scope at each call site (it's already threaded through addCommonParams in Session 3 — see commit 1e4e60d). This wrapping is the natural seam for per-call path/method awareness without touching the embassy layer. Same pattern as the addCommonParams hook from Session 3, just on the response side.

title: sync: investigate identifier inventory
description: Spike. Narrowed to visitorId only (contactId is out of scope by design: SDK never knows it; server resolves from the 4-id set and/or the access token, algorithm.md:73-80, :260-267). Confirm the Brevo sib_cuid cookie name and read path on Web, plus normalization rules. In the pilot critical path because the contact pilot sends 4 identifiers including visitorId.
design: See plan at /Users/stephane.jais/.claude/plans/read-this-users-stephane-jais-work-brevo-imperative-nest.md and source docs at /Users/stephane.jais/Work/Brevo/sdk-sync/docs/docs/sync/. SDK exploration found that contactId and visitorId do not currently exist in the SDK (verified in src/wonderpush/session.js and src/wonderpush/init.js).
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in beads notes for: cookie name and read path for visitorId on Web, plus normalization rules.
notes:
SPIKE DECISION (recorded 2026-06-15).

COOKIE NAME: 'sib_cuid' (also called CUID). Value = UUID v4, lowercase hex, hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12.
Sources: sdk-sync docs CLAUDE.md:55 ('Visitor IDs (a UUID v4 cookie on the Web also called CUID or sib_cuid)'); Brevo tracker wrapper hl.prototype.gen_sib_cuid generates lowercase UUID v4 via 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx'.replace(...).toString(16).

READ PATH (Web): the cookie is read with WonderPushSDK._protected.Helper.cookie.get('sib_cuid') — defined at embassy/src/embassy/helper.js:13 (splits document.cookie on ';', trims leading spaces, matches 'sib_cuid=', returns decodeURIComponent of the value, or '' if absent). The SDK ALREADY reads it this way in 3 places: notification.js:1122, installation.js:539, installation-profile.js:414.

RECOMMENDED for 71i + Sync.identifiers(): do NOT read document.cookie directly. Reuse the existing RunMode-aware accessor WonderPushSDK._protected.Installation.Profile.getVisitorId (installation-profile.js:409): on ModeWebSite it reads Helper.cookie.get('sib_cuid'); on ModeFrame it delegates to the parent window via Integration.callOnParentWindow; it persists/falls back to the 'device.visitorId' core property. This matches the proxified-identifier-accessor rule (memory reference-sdk-identifier-accessors) so it works across RunModes (Popup/Frame iframes).

NORMALIZATION RULES:
- Helper.cookie.get returns '' (empty string) when the cookie is absent. Treat '' (and undefined) as 'no visitorId' → OMIT visitorId from the wire (buildOutgoingParams/buildExplicitFetchParams already skip falsy/undefined identifiers).
- The value is already canonical (lowercase hyphenated UUID v4 from gen_sib_cuid); no case-folding or reformatting required. decodeURIComponent + leading-space trim are applied by cookie.get; for a UUID these are no-ops.
- No prefix/wrapping: the raw UUID is the identifier (the tracker sends it raw as 'cuid' and 'visitor_id').

TIMING: the wrapper generates+sets sib_cuid synchronously (Helper.cookie.set) BEFORE it appends the async WonderPush SDK <script> (wonderPushTracker()). So sib_cuid is reliably present by the time the SDK runs — no need to wait/poll for it on first load.

GAPS / FOLLOW-UPS for 71i:
- Popup RunMode: Installation.Profile.getVisitorId handles ModeWebSite + ModeFrame but not Popup explicitly (falls through to core-property default). Verify Popup reads via parent like Frame, or document the limitation.
- Service Worker context: no document.cookie; Helper.cookie.get is unsafe there. visitorId must be omitted in SW run mode.
- contactId: OUT OF SCOPE by design (server resolves it; algorithm.md:73-80, :260-267).
close_reason: Spike complete: cookie name (sib_cuid, lowercase UUID v4), read path (Helper.cookie.get / Installation.Profile.getVisitorId RunMode-aware accessor), and normalization rules ('' = absent → omit; no reformatting) recorded in notes with sources. SDK already reads sib_cuid in 3 places; reuse the existing accessor for 71i.

title: sync+inapp: on @APP_OPEN, wait for the contact AND popups sync to settle before evaluating in-apps
description:
@APP_OPEN (on Web: @VISIT translated to @APP_OPEN, automatic-actions.ts:33-36) fires a POST /events that piggybacks the opportunistic sdk-sync params. That response (and any explicit GET it triggers) can deliver, for THIS cycle:
  - fresh CONTACT data — which now feeds local segmentation (5ar): a popup whose segment references contact fields must be evaluated against the just-synced contact, not a stale one.
  - new/updated POPUPS themselves, once the popups source lands (fpk).

Today the in-app engine only waits, on @APP_OPEN, for the remote-config version to settle (InAppMessaging.getEventDelayPromise, main.ts:136-185: <10s-old config => immediate; else wait up to 5s for RemoteConfigVersionDeclared(not new) or RemoteConfigUpdated, else timeout). It does NOT wait for the sync channel at all. So on this @APP_OPEN cycle a popup could be evaluated against stale contact data (wrong match decision) or miss a sync-delivered popup, only correcting on the next trigger.

Goal: on @APP_OPEN, also wait (bounded, like the config wait) for the sync of EACH relevant registered source — contact AND popups — to settle before InAppMessaging evaluates in-apps/popups.

Proposed mechanism (mirrors the existing config-version wait; generic over source):
1. sync.js emits a broadcast when a source's processing for a response cycle settles — SyncSourceSettled with data { source }. 'Settled' = the opportunistic response needed no explicit fetch for that source, OR a triggered explicit fetch completed (success or give-up). Uses WonderPushSDK._protected.Integration.broadcast (config.js:56 / remote-config.ts:329).
2. InAppMessaging.getEventDelayPromise('@APP_OPEN') gains a per-source gate for each ACTIVE source in { contact, popups }: wait for SyncSourceSettled{source} alongside the existing config gate. Resolve when ALL armed gates (config + each active source) are satisfied, or the existing maxDelay (5s) timeout fires. Reuse this.integration.addBroadcastListener/removeBroadcastListener (main.ts:180-181).
3. Arm a source's gate only when that source is active (Sync.getRegisteredSources() includes it AND opportunistic injection enabled); otherwise that gate is pre-satisfied. So the CONTACT gate arms now (contact pilot exists), the POPUPS gate arms when fpk ships, and with no sync at all behavior is unchanged.
4. Revisit the <10s 'brand new config' fast-path (main.ts:141): it returns immediately today; with sync gating it should still wait on the armed source gates (fresh config doesn't imply the contact/popups sync has settled).
acceptance_criteria:
1. On @APP_OPEN, for EACH active source in {contact, popups}, evaluation is delayed until that source's SyncSourceSettled broadcast OR the shared maxDelay timeout — never longer than maxDelay total.
2. The config-version gate is preserved; config + contact + popups gates COMPOSE (proceed once all armed gates settle, or timeout).
3. A source whose gate is not armed (source not registered / sync disabled) is treated as pre-satisfied; with no sync at all, getEventDelayPromise('@APP_OPEN') behaves exactly as today.
4. Non-@APP_OPEN events are unaffected (resolve immediately).
5. A popup is evaluated against the contact data synced on THIS @APP_OPEN (not the previous cycle's), within maxDelay; and a popup delivered by the sync response is eligible on the same cycle.
6. sync.js emits SyncSourceSettled in both the no-fetch-needed and fetch-completed cases, and on give-up, so no gate can hang past maxDelay.
notes: The CONTACT gate is implementable NOW — the contact source plug-in exists (n3q) and contact feeds segmentation (5ar, shipped). The POPUPS gate needs the popups source (fpk) + GET /popups (ki1). Consider implementing the generic SyncSourceSettled mechanism + the contact gate ahead of fpk (the fpk dep here blocks only the popups portion). Touch points: sync.js consumeIncomingResponse / runFetchWithMutexHeld (emit settled), new SyncSourceSettledBroadcastType, src/inappmessaging/main.ts getEventDelayPromise. Broadcast plumbing exists (main.ts:170-181). Origin: 2026-06-18 popups design; amended 2026-06-24 to include contact (now relevant via 5ar).
close_reason: Implemented. sync-broadcasts.ts (SyncSourceSettled type); sync.js emits SyncSourceSettled{source} when a source settles (no pending fetch) + on fetch give-up; main.ts getEventDelayPromise composes the config gate with per-source gates for armed {contact, popups}, bounded by the 5s maxDelay, with the <10s fast-path still awaiting sync gates; armed only when registered (unchanged when sync absent); wonderpush.d.ts Sync gains getRegisteredSources. Typecheck clean, 221 sync+inapp tests pass. Test gap: behavioral test of the gate needs an InAppMessaging/main.ts harness (none exists) — deferred.

title: sync: plug contact source data into the popups (inapp) local segmentation engine
description:
Make synced contact data (sdk-sync 'contact' source) usable as an input to local in-app/popup segmentation, so popups can be targeted on contact fields client-side.

NOTE: contact != user. The segmentation engine (src/inappmessaging/segmenter.ts) already models a UserSource (the WonderPush user object), with visitUserSource returning [] (segmenter.ts:428) and the join path treating a user context as unsupported. That is the USER, a different entity. There is NO ContactSource in the segmentation DSL (notiflex-segmentation-dsl-parser) today — grep confirms zero 'contact' references. A contact data source must be created.

SCOPE CAVEAT: the 2way-sync architecture plan currently lists 'Popup-engine consumption of synced rules' as explicitly out of scope (plan lines 7, 139). This issue is the follow-up that takes that on, per user direction (2026-06-16) to create a ContactSource.

Where the contact data lives: the contact source plug-in stores the contact object in its per-source state.data (sync-contact.js:53, sync-contact-store.ts), keyed sync:contact:<userId>:<deviceId> (sync-state.ts:49). The Sync module currently exposes getRegisteredSources() and identifiers() but NO public accessor to read a source's current data — one must be added.

Work spans three layers:
  1. DSL parser (notiflex-segmentation-dsl-parser, external dep): add a ContactSource node + visitContactSource to ASTCriterionVisitor. Likely an upstream change to that package, then bump the version here.
  2. segmenter.ts: add a ContactVisitor (BaseVisitor subclass) whose visitFieldSource resolves field paths against the contact object; implement visitContactSource; add a ContactSource branch in visitJoinCriterionNode (alongside the existing InstallationSource/EventSource/CurrentUrlSource branches, ~lines 259-283); thread a contactData param through the Segmenter constructor and the nested visitor constructions.
  3. Wiring: add a Sync read accessor for the contact source data; in automatic-actions.ts:85-111 fetch it (alongside installation.getProperties() etc.) and pass it into new Segmenter(...).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A ContactSource exists in the segmentation DSL and parses in a segment expression referencing contact fields.
2. Segmenter evaluates contact-field criteria against the synced contact object (state.data of the contact source), returning correct match/no-match for equality, presence, prefix/suffix/contains, and nested field paths — mirroring InstallationVisitor's field semantics.
3. Contact data is read via a Sync accessor (not by reaching into storage keys directly) and survives the proxified RunMode accessor pattern.
4. A segment with NO contact criteria still behaves exactly as today (no regression in segmenter.test.ts).
5. contact and user remain distinct: a UserSource criterion is unaffected by contact data and vice-versa.
6. Behaviour is gated so that when no contact data is present (source never synced) the engine degrades gracefully (empty -> field criteria do not match, consistent with installation-absent behaviour).

External-dep work: notiflex-segmentation-dsl-parser needs the ContactSource node — coordinate an upstream release + version bump. Construction site: automatic-actions.ts:103. Field-resolution reference implementation: InstallationVisitor.visitFieldSource (segmenter.ts:482-522), including the custom date_ coercion. Filed 2026-06-16; conflicts with current plan exclusion (lines 7,139) — plan should be updated if this is greenlit for the roadmap.

title: sync: GET /v1/popups explicit endpoint integration
description: Wire Sync.fetch('popups') to GET /v1/popups with 4 identifier params (userId/installationId/deviceId/visitorId) + lastSync* + known*. Demoted from PILOT critical path 2026-06-11. Source name 'popups' matches the URL path; on the wire the explicit response's source block lives at the response root. Route the top-level response through the multi-object processor: full data:[] is a reset (only when lastVersion==0 per algorithm.md:301), delta:[] is an array of full objects merged by id favoring highest version, tombstones (status=='deleted') kept until expirationDate. Explicit paging semantics (algorithm.md:299-301): the response's version/versionId = the Nth (last-of-page) item's update date / id, NOT the highest. knownVersion/knownVersionId carry the head beyond this page. Paging converges when knownVersion/knownVersionId are no longer strictly higher than the response's version/versionId. The SDK loops the explicit fetch advancing lastVersion/lastVersionId until convergence.
design: Algorithm.md 'For sources that are a list of items' branch in the explicit endpoint section.
acceptance_criteria: Firm hint in opportunistic response triggers GET /v1/popups; multi-page paging via knownVersion/knownVersionId converges to a fully-synced list; dedupe and tombstone retention exercised by integration tests.
close_reason: Implemented together. fpk: multi-object popups store (sync-popups-store.ts: reset/merge-by-id-favoring-highest-updateDate/tombstone-retention/prune) + sync-popups.js plug-in + registered in wonderpush.js. ki1: GET /v1/popups paging via the existing Sync.fetch('popups'); processor emits continuePaging on the explicit path while the head exceeds the applied page version; sync.js pages from the advanced cursor (fires after save), exempts paging from the 9vn floor, and block-acquires the mutex so no page is dropped. Implements: list dedupe-by-id favoring highest version; full data:[] reset semantics; multi-object delta is an ARRAY OF FULL OBJECTS merged into the stored list by id (algorithm.md:154, merged-vs-separated-lists.md:40-41); soft-delete tombstone retention (status=='deleted') until expirationDate (sources.md:179). Multi-identifier query: sends 4 identifiers — never contactId. Opportunistic responses for multi-object carry NO data/delta — only hints (algorithm.md:120-121). Explicit response carries data:[] ONLY when lastVersion==0 (algorithm.md:301), otherwise only delta:[].
